q: 1. Most commonly used solvent in oil paints, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: turpentine is also very widely used as a thinner in oil paints, so this key answer is debatable.

q: 2. Plastic asphalt is
options: used as a water proofing layer over roof
a mixture of cement and asphalt
explain: Plastic asphalt, being flexible and impermeable, is applied as a waterproofing layer over roofs.

q: 3. Varnish is a transparent or semi-transparent solution of resinous substances in .....
explain: Varnish can be made by dissolving resins in alcohol (spirit varnish), linseed oil (oil varnish) or turpentine (turpentine varnish).

q: 4. The oil/liquid in which base and pigment are dissolved to form paint is called
explain: The vehicle is the liquid medium (usually oil) that carries and binds the base and pigment together in paint.

q: 5. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is .....
explain: Red lead is a rust-inhibiting pigment, so it is used where corrosion resistance is needed.

q: 6. The magnesium refractories material can withstand
explain: Magnesium-based refractories (like Magnesite) are basic refractories capable of withstanding extreme furnace temperatures.

q: 7. The main ingredient in the manufacture of glass is .....
explain: Silica (sand) is the main constituent of glass.

q: 8. The type of glass used in glazing the north light trusses is .....
explain: Wired glass is strong and holds together if broken, so it is used for north light glazing.

q: 9. The asbestos content in asbestos cement sheets is roughly about .....
explain: As per the answer key, asbestos cement sheets contain roughly 15% asbestos.

q: 10. Polymerization helps to improve the property of
explain: Polymerization forms long-chain molecular structures that enhance strength, rigidity, and elasticity of materials like polymers.

q: 11. The most fire resistant, paints are .....
explain: Asbestos paints are the most fire resistant since asbestos does not burn.

q: 12. The most durable varnish is .....
explain: Oil varnish forms a tough, durable film and is the most durable type.

q: 13. A constituent of paint that helps in quick drying of painted surface is
explain: A drier is added to paint specifically to speed up the oxidation/drying process of the film.

q: 14. A thinner used in distemper is
explain: Since distemper is a water-based paint, water itself is used as the thinner to adjust its consistency.

q: 15. Thinner used for oil paint is
explain: Turpentine is the standard thinner used to reduce the viscosity of oil-based paints.

q: 16. The paint having white lead or zinc white as base mixed in oil with petroleum spirit and resinous matter is known as
explain: Enamel paint is formed by combining a white lead/zinc white base with oil, spirit, and resin, producing a hard glossy finish.

q: 17. The colour of asphalt is
options: deep black with slight tinge of redness
explain: Asphalt is generally described as black-brownish in color, distinguishing it visually from other bituminous materials.

q: 18. Coal-tar is obtained by destructive distillation of
explain: Coal-tar is a byproduct obtained from the destructive (high-temperature, air-free) distillation of coal.

q: 19. Bitumen felt is used for
explain: Bitumen felt is impermeable and flexible, making it ideal for waterproofing and damp-proofing applications.

q: 20. In paints, pigment is responsible for .....
explain: Pigments give paint its colour.

q: 21. The base in a paint is added to .....
options: hide the surface to be painted
explain: As per the answer key, the base gives the paint body and opacity so it hides the surface to be painted.

q: 22. Asphalt is a good insulator of
explain: Asphalt, being a dense hydrocarbon-mineral composite, insulates well against heat, sound, and electrical conduction.

q: 23. The commonly used extender in a paint is .....
explain: As per the answer key, any one of these. Barium sulphate and gypsum are extenders, and alcohol is included in the book's key answer.

q: 24. The drier in an oil paint should not be more than ..... (by volume).
explain: As per the answer key, driers should not exceed 10% by volume.

q: 25. For providing windscreen of cars, buses and other automobile vehicles, the glass used is
explain: Laminated glass, with a plastic interlayer, holds together on impact and is used for automobile windscreens for safety.

q: 26. Asphalt is a
options: mixture of bitumen and inert material
explain: Asphalt is a mixture of bitumen with inert mineral matter such as sand or limestone dust.

q: 27. French polish is a kind of
explain: French polish is a type of spirit varnish made by dissolving shellac in alcohol/spirit.

q: 28. Lithophone is
options: an oxide of iron used as a base
explain: Lithopone is a white pigment composed of zinc sulfide and barium sulfate, used as an alternative to white lead.

q: 29. The basic purpose of a retarder in concrete is
options: to increase the initial setting time of cement paste in concrete
to decrease the initial setting time of cement paste in concrete
to render the concrete more water tight
to improve the workability of concrete mix
explain: A retarder is added specifically to extend (increase) the initial setting time, giving more working time before the concrete sets.

q: 30. PVC stands for
explain: PVC is the common abbreviation for polyvinyl chloride, a widely used plastic polymer.

q: 31. The pigment in paints gives
explain: The primary role of the pigment is to provide color and hide the surface being painted.

q: 32. The base material for distemper is
explain: Chalk (whiting) is the primary base material used in the preparation of distemper.

q: 33. Distemper is a mixture of
explain: Basic distemper consists of powdered chalk mixed with water and a binder (like glue/size).

q: 34. Lacquer paints are
options: are more durable compared to enamel paints
explain: Lacquers are high-performance coatings often containing nitrocellulose and resins, known for their durability on metal surfaces.

q: 35. Lacquer is
explain: Lacquers are technically a type of spirit varnish that dries by evaporation of the solvent.

q: 36. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surfaces not exposed to weather
explain: Distemper is not weather-resistant and is primarily used for interior walls (interior plastered surfaces).

q: 37. The best primer used for structural steel/iron is
explain: Red lead is the most effective primer for steel as it provides excellent corrosion resistance.

q: 38. The function of a paint is
options: to increase the life of the surface
explain: Paint serves both aesthetic (appearance) and protective (corrosion/weathering) functions.

q: 39. The paints used in aircrafts are
explain: Cellulose paints (lacquers) are used for aircraft because they dry very rapidly by evaporation and provide a hard, smooth, and flexible surface.

q: 40. The varnish is essentially made of
explain: Varnish consists of a resin dissolved in a solvent (and sometimes oil) to allow for application and film formation.

q: 41. PVC stands for
explain: In the context of paint technology, PVC refers to the Pigment Volume Concentration.

q: 42. The cracks developed throughout thickness of paint due various reason is known as
explain: Cracking involves deep breaks in the paint film that often expose the underlying surface.

q: 43. Brilliant varnish is
explain: Spirit varnishes (like French polish) dry quickly to a very high, brilliant gloss.

q: 44. Bitumen is generally obtained form
explain: Bitumen is a fractional distillation product of crude petroleum.

q: 45. Bitumen emulsion is
options: a liquid containing bitumen in suspension
explain: An emulsion is a mixture where fine droplets of bitumen are suspended in water with the help of an emulsifying agent.

q: 46. Bitumen felt is
explain: Bitumen felt (rolls of fabric impregnated with bitumen) is used widely for both damp proofing and roof waterproofing.

q: 47. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surface not exposed to weather
explain: Distemper is a water-based interior finish that is not suitable for surfaces exposed to rain or sun.
